_doc: A cohort boundary is NOT always a prompt bump. The agentic arm's query_prices
returned [] from deploy (the substrate was never packaged), so the arm was
PRICE-BLIND while carrying prompt_version daily_agentic/v1 the whole time —
by_prompt_version cannot see that boundary, because the prompt never changed.
STAMPED vs PENDING (T-351). `from_date` is a CONFIRMED, stamped fact. `pending_from`
is an ANNOUNCED deploy that has not been confirmed yet. They are different states and
collapsing them makes the registry assert something false: once the fix is live, the
default 'price_blind' stops being an honest default and becomes a silent MISLABEL of
rows the arm could actually see prices for. A row on/after `pending_from` with no
`from_date` is labelled `price_fed_UNSTAMPED` — an explicit 'not vouched for yet',
never a confident claim. Resolving that explicit unknown when E stamps the date is a
RESOLUTION, not a retroactive reinterpretation: the never-reinterpret rule protects
SETTLED claims (a price_blind row stays blind forever), not declared unknowns.
2026-09-10, director merge: A's T-351 schema and E's stamp landed in the same cycle;
this file carries BOTH — the schema, with the price_fed boundary STAMPED. A stamped
boundary always wins over a pending one; pending_from is retained as the announcement

cohorts.label: price_blind
cohorts.note: query_prices returned [] since deploy — the arm could not see prices at all; closes 2026-09-10 inclusive (the 09-10 run used jobdef :32, verified from the Batch record)

cohorts.label: price_fed
cohorts.note: STAMPED BY E 2026-09-10 as a fact, not a plan. rev33 (paper-sha-7021abc) deployed the afternoon of 2026-09-10 and was verified IN-CONTAINER before deploy: query_prices returns 50 rows where it returned 0. The date is 2026-09-11, NOT the deploy date itself, and the distinction is the whole point of the label rule: the 2026-09-10 agentic run fired at 08:45 CDT on jobdef archondex-paper-cloud-day:32 — the PRE-rev33 image — which is provable from the Batch record, so that row was written price-BLIND. Stamping 09-10 would have let a price-blind row wear the price_fed label. The first run that can see prices is the 2026-09-11 09:45 ET pulse.
cohorts.pending_note: rev33 deployed 2026-09-10 (query_prices 0 -> 50 rows); book window opens 2026-09-11. Announcement record; superseded by the stamped from_date above.
cohorts.treatment_caveat: WHAT THE LABEL IS WORTH, as distinct from when it starts. The arm in this era can HONESTLY QUERY a price substrate that ends 2026-05-22 — verified on the first price_fed note, which asked for recent SPY prices and correctly got zero rows. So the era's actual treatment is 'can query a stale research substrate', which is close to NO TREATMENT. A price_fed-era A/B read measures a nearly-empty treatment and should surprise nobody by showing nothing; it is NOT evidence that the agentic design does not work. The real treatment begins with the live-price cohort.
cohorts.caveat_note: Kept in its own field: the `note` above is a stamped record of a FACT (when the label starts) and must stay byte-identical. This is INTERPRETATION (what the label is worth) and may be revised without ever touching the stamped fact.
